# Porting conventions (read before writing any code)

This is a **from-scratch rewrite in C** of the DOS game Yogho Yogho, faithful to the original in
gameplay. The specification is the teardown in `..\extracted\teardown\` (00-BRIEFING first).
Every ported routine must be traceable to the original: cite the Ghidra address in a comment at
the top of the function and at non-obvious lines. **No tuning by eye, no guessing**: if the spec
is unclear, read the instructions (`..\extracted\ghidra\disasm_fixed.txt`, overlay listings in
`..\extracted\ovl_dis\`, capstone via `..\scripts\dis16.py` / `exe_dis.py` / `ovl_dis.py`), and if
still unclear, implement the most literal reading and list it under "open questions" in your report.

## Memory model (`src/mem.h`)
- All game state lives in `MEM` (1 MB real-mode memory) at the **original addresses**: the EXE
  image (with relocations) is loaded at runtime segment `0x0824` (Ghidra `1000`), DGROUP is at
  `0x226A` (Ghidra `2a46`). Runtime segment = Ghidra segment − 0x7DC; use `SEG_G(0x160a)` etc.
- DGROUP access: `DB(off)` byte lvalue, `dgw(off)` / `dgw_set(off,v)` words, `dgs(off)` signed.
  Other memory: `rb/rw/wb/ww(seg, off)` (these route A000–AFFF to the VGA model). `P(seg,off)` gives a
  raw pointer — never for VRAM.
- Initialised tables (strings, level descriptors, frame tables, collision shapes, CS-resident
  tables…) are **read from MEM** (they come from the user's YOGHO.EXE), never retyped.
- Self-modified CS variables (e.g. CS:1011, CS:101f, CS:3b7a) are kept as words in MEM at
  `SEG_EXE:offset` exactly like the original, so dumps line up.
- Loaded data (DAT entries) goes where the original puts it (segments held in DGROUP like
  `[0x13fe]`, `[0x1402]`, `[0x2cda]`…), via `dat_load(idx, off, seg)`.
- Integer semantics: use `uint16_t`/`int16_t`/`uint8_t`/`int8_t` exactly as the asm does (wrap,
  signed vs unsigned compares, CBW, carries via explicit 32-bit adds). Byte vs word stores matter.

## Calling conventions (`src/cpu.h`, `src/game.h`)
- **REG** routines (asm with register args — engine helpers, all 26 API slots, every overlay
  handler): `void name(void)`, arguments and results in the global `Regs R` (`R.ax`, `R.bx`, …,
  `R.es`, `R.ds`, flags `R.cf/R.zf/R.sf` where the caller tests them). Preserve/clobber registers
  as the original does only where a caller depends on it (document it).
- **C** routines (Borland cdecl, mostly segment 160a; blitters with stack args): normal C params
  in original order; far pointers as `(off, seg)`; return AX (32-bit results also put DX in `R.dx`).
- `game.h` is the contract: it declares every cross-module routine with its owner. **Do not edit
  `game.h`.** If you need to export more, declare it in your own header `src/<module>_ext.h` and
  mention it in your report; the lead merges.
- Dynamic far calls through data (object handlers `CALLF [slot+0]`, overlay entry `CALLF [2d66]`,
  compiled sprites) go through `farcall(seg, off)` (`src/farcall.c`). Overlay modules register
  handlers per level with `farcall_register_overlay(level_index, offset, fn)` inside
  `ovl_register_all()`-reachable init functions; engine routines reachable through data pointers
  register with `farcall_register_exe(ghidra_seg, off, fn)`.
- Near calls/jumps between ported routines are plain C calls; a tail `jmp stub` to an API slot is a
  call followed by `return`.

## Hardware
- VGA: port I/O with `io_out(port, v)` / `io_outw(port, ax)` (= `OUT DX,AX`) / `io_in(port)`;
  VRAM by `wb/rb(0xA000+.., off)`. The model (`src/vga.c`) implements map mask, read map,
  write modes 0/1 + latches, CRTC start/offset/line compare, pel panning, DAC. Port the asm's
  writes literally (plane order, map-mask words) — that keeps output pixel-identical.
- Retrace polling (`IN 3DAh`) always reports "in retrace". Any original busy-wait on a counter
  that the ISR changes becomes a loop with `plat_yield()` (see `wait_ticks`, `spin_while_*` in
  `src/isr.c`). Never busy-wait without yielding.
- AdLib: done (`src/adlib.c`). Timer ISR / keyboard / waits: done (`src/isr.c`).
- Mouse (int 33h) and joystick: the flow module owns them (platform gives `plat_mouse()`).

## Build / check
- `./check.sh src/yourfile.c ...` compiles your files only (MSVC, C11) — use it constantly; it
  must be warning-clean for your files. `./b.sh` builds the whole program (will only link once
  all modules exist).
- Style: C11, 4-space indent, match `src/adlib.c` / `src/isr.c`. Comment density like those files.
- Do not run the original game or DOSBox. Do not touch files outside your module list.

# reference/

Public-domain source material, checked in.

Everything in this directory is here because it can be redistributed. That is
the opposite of `fixtures/amiga/` and `data/`, which are Commodore and
SoftVoice's and are gitignored.

## `nrl-7948.json`

The 329 letter-to-sound rules of:

> H. S. Elovitz, R. W. Johnson, A. McHugh and J. E. Shore,
> *Automatic Translation of English Text to Phonetics by Means of
> Letter-to-Sound Rules*, NRL Report 7948 (AD/A021 929),
> Naval Research Laboratory, Washington DC, 21 January 1976.

A work of the United States Government, and so not subject to copyright in the
United States (17 U.S.C. 105). Scans are available from DTIC as `ADA021929`.

The rule strings are a transcription of the report's appendix. 320 of the 329
were confirmed verbatim against OCR of the scanned report; the other 9 are
present but OCR-damaged. The character-class and metacharacter definitions
alongside them are from the report's SNOBOL listing. See
`research/03-nrl-provenance.md` for the verification and for the diff against
the Amiga table.

Used by `tools/nrl-diff.py` and `tools/gen-nrl-table.py`.

## `formants.json`

The measured formant frequencies of ten American English vowels:

> G. E. Peterson and H. L. Barney, *Control Methods Used in a Study of the
> Vowels*, Journal of the Acoustical Society of America 24(2), 175-184, 1952.
> Table II, adult male means.

Measurements are facts rather than expression, and these particular ones have
been reproduced in every phonetics textbook since. They are here because
33.2's own vowel table appears to have been built from them: read back through
`tools/formants.py --diff`, its `IY` lands within one Hz of the published
`270 / 2290 / 3010`, and `AO`'s third formant is exact. 25 of 30 values agree
within 10%.

That matters for the free voice. Rebuilding the vowels from this table is not
an approximation of what SoftVoice did — it is the same thing they did, from
the same source.

## `nrl-table.json`

The same rules, built into the shape the library loads — a `TranslatorTables`,
interchangeable with the extracted Amiga ones. This is the free table: usable
without permission from anyone.

```sh
python3 tools/gen-nrl-table.py --check data/translator-33.2.json
```

Generated rather than hand-written, and checked in anyway, because everything
it derives from is in this directory. Its character-class table is rebuilt
from the report's SNOBOL class definitions, not lifted from a binary; `--check`
diffs it against a real build, and they agree on every bit the matcher reads.

It has no stress marks, no whole-word pronunciations and no letter-name rules,
because NRL has none of those. Ignoring stress, about two thirds of English
words come out identical to `translator.library` 33.2 —
`npx vite-node tools/nrl-divergence.ts` measures it.

## `voice-free.json`

A complete narrator voice built by `tools/gen-free-voice.py` from published
phonetics and from what `research/02-narrator.md` established each table
column means. Nothing in it is Commodore's or SoftVoice's.

The rule the generator holds to:

> Measurements come from the literature, cited at the point of use.
> Structure comes from principle, with the reasoning written down.
> No number is ever copied out of an extracted table.

It is not byte-identical to 33.2 and is not trying to be. What it is checked
against is stated rather than assumed — the attribute words, derived from
phonetic features alone, agree with 33.2's on 98% of their bits, and an
utterance comes out within 7% of the same length.

Texture, against the same utterance — `tools/voice-texture.py` reproduces it:

| | 33.2 | free |
|---|---|---|
| spectral centroid | 2517 Hz | 2380 Hz |
| energy above 4 kHz | 22.9% | 20.4% |
| roughness | 0.18 | 0.18 |
| zero crossings | 390 Hz | 387 Hz |
| RMS / peak | 25.7 / 122 | 26.8 / 122 |

It was much harsher than that, and then it was clear but slurred — "please
top what you want me to se". Six things were wrong, and all six were
structural rather than a matter of taste:

- **The amplitude scale was linear where it should have been decibels.** The
  stored value controls a 5-bit multiplier, so the widest range it can express
  is 30 dB and the 31 steps across it are ~1 dB each. Once `gain_curve()`
  became the antilog of that, it came out within a step of 33.2's own curve at
  every point — the same agreement the vowel formants have, and for the same
  reason.
- **The formant levels came from a truncated pole product.** Three poles keep
  every skirt from below and lose every lift from above, which costs 20 dB at
  F3 and puts /IY/'s F2 under the floor — the vowel loses the formant that
  identifies it, and the diphthong glides go with it, which is what turned
  *type* into *top*. Carried to convergence with the tract's higher poles at
  their neutral positions, the model lands 2.9 dB from 33.2's own table on
  average.
- **The noise tables were filtered per byte, and the renderer reads two
  samples out of every byte.** Whatever shaping went in was destroyed by the
  split; every table measured the same, and all of them far too loud.
- **`QX` had a vowel's amplitudes.** It is the placeholder the pitch stage
  seeds a slot with, so every utterance began with a buzz.
- **The excitation used a third of the five bits available**, which quantises
  a vowel to three and puts broadband hash under all of it. It also decayed
  from the pitch pulse when the pulse is the glottal *opening*: the second
  half of every period came out nearly silent, peaky enough to force the whole
  voice's level down to stay inside eight bits. Modelling both halves — the
  ring-down of the last pulse plus Rosenberg's rising flow of the current one
  — put the crest factor within 0.1 dB of 33.2's.
- **There were no rewrite rules at all**, which I had written off as missing
  polish. It is not: the driver runs the engine twice, and the second pass is
  what expands a phoneme into the several slots it is really stored as. A
  diphthong's offglide and a stop's release live in the blank slots after
  their nucleus, and only the nucleus is in the inventory the parser matches.
  Without the rules, every diphthong in the language was its nucleus alone —
  *type* came out *top*, *say* came out *se*, and *five* was unrecognisable.
  Which slot follows which is a fact about the table layout rather than a
  choice, so the free set comes out much the same shape as 33.2's: 42 frame
  rules against its 46.

- **A stop's closure made noise.** Frication belongs to the slots the frame
  rules append, not to the slot that names the phoneme — a closure is silence,
  which is the whole of what makes a stop a stop. Putting the frication on the
  head turns /CH/ into /SH/ and takes the stop out of every stop. The release
  slots had the opposite problem: no formants and no amplitude at all, so the
  vowel after a stop had to interpolate up from silence.

## `wordlist.txt`

88 monosyllables covering the vowel inventory and the consonants in onset and
coda, for `tools/intelligibility.py`. Ordinary English words, chosen for
coverage; nothing in the list is anybody's property.

**This is the measurement that matters, and it is the one that is failing.**
Whisper, given each word inside a carrier phrase, scores:

| | |
|---|---|
| 33.2 voice, 33.2 letter-to-sound | 35/88 = 40% |
| free voice, 33.2 letter-to-sound | 16/88 = 18% |
| free voice, free letter-to-sound | 9/88 = 10% |

Everything above the second row is the voice; the gap between the second and
third is the letter-to-sound table, which has no stress marks and so gives the
prosody stages nothing to work with.
That gap is invisible to `voice-texture.py`, which has the two agreeing to
within a few percent on centroid, roughness and high-frequency share — sounding
like 33.2 and being as intelligible as 33.2 are different properties, and only
the second one matters.

What is still missing is the *contextual* allophony — the flapped /t/ of
"butter", and the rest of 33.2's 33-rule first pass. The free set has seven:
the six syllabic consonants and dark /l/. It speaks; it is not finished.

# Current status

Updated 2026-10-25.

## Modern championship

`remaster.html` supports all ten original circuits, a ten-car field with original named rivals/models, a saved season calendar and standings, original place prizes, contracts, repairs and live pits. Guns, lasers, particle beams, Terminator rockets and homing missiles are selectable. Ordnance includes original prices/capacities, upgrades, pit rearming, target locks, incoming warnings, braking evasion and interception. A championship win carries equipment and cash into a harder season; a loss ends the season. Any city can be selected in separate practice. The game uses continuous 60 Hz arcade handling and Babylon rendering. All weapon families and the first ten-city landmark pass are implemented; exact rival behavior, human championship balance and release validation remain open. Seattle now has worn asphalt, overcast lighting and improved shadows, with textured race cars and pooled smoke/explosions shared across the remaster. Persistent weather and time-of-day presets add a procedural sky, cloud drift, rain, wet asphalt and fog across remaster circuits. Automatic weather now holds conditions for 60 seconds and blends over 20 seconds; manual changes blend over eight seconds. Street-lamp arms and lenses now face the road. An independent six-minute automatic day/night cycle fades headlights and nearby street spotlights on at dusk, with fewer local lights on Balanced. Filtered local-light shadows now let cars and road/overpass structures block headlights and street lights. High uses up to six 512px maps, Balanced four 256px maps; inactive lights stop refreshing. Focused New York/Boston comparisons confirmed crossing occlusion. Rain now stops on road/roof surfaces and creates pooled ripples. Effects volume controls sheltered rain ambience and delayed thunder accompanying occasional cloud lightning; reduced motion suppresses flashes. Short local rain/combat stress samples held 60 fps on High and Balanced with the mirror enabled; a 20-minute local ten-city rain/night rendering soak and post-fix Balanced regression are complete. Balanced lamp handoffs now stay within four shadows. Full-race AI/physics checks are complete across all ten circuits: 90 independent fixed-step scenarios (6.13 simulated hours), all 50 three-lap practice finishes and all 280 pit services, with no stalls or invalid states detected. Career scenarios ended in seven finishes and 33 wrecks; human championship survival/economy balance remains open. Live pit transactions exposed and verified a fix for a $1 floating-point repair overcharge. Representative-hardware, multi-hour and human championship checks remain pending. See [full-race results](remaster-full-race-checks.md). See [performance measurements](remaster-weather-performance.md). See [remaster scope and controls](remaster.md).

## Track editor

`editor.html` provides Circuit Lab: road/elevation editing, scenery placement, linked profile, lap marker preview, undo/redo, local drafts, project import/export and binary TRK export. All ten original tracks round-trip byte-identically. The preview is schematic, not a game simulation; custom track drivability requires playtesting. See [the editor guide](track-editor.md).

## Supported build

- `DTRACK.EXE`, SHA-256 `5b23cafb…ff2928`: Deathtrack 1.0 (1989) PC, with the one-byte copy-protection patch. Asset set: `src/data/manifest.json` (92 files).
- Display: EGA mode 0Dh (default, the adapter DOSBox detects), or CGA with `?video=cga` (argument `GC`: the game sets BIOS mode 6, 640x200 two colours, dithered; the driver programs mode 4 first).
- Sound: PC-speaker path by default (music and effects), rendered in the browser by an AudioWorklet from time-stamped PIT/port 61h changes. The browser test asserts non-silent output. Audio fidelity (speaker response) is APPROX and has not been compared with hardware or DOSBox output.
- Browser default sound is `mt32` (built-in synth fallback); `?sound=speaker` selects the PC speaker. Optional music hardware: `?sound=adlib` (OPL2 register stream rendered by `src/engine/opl2.js`, an independent APPROX synth; effects stay on the speaker) and `?sound=mt32` (MPU-401 UART, MIDI bytes sent to a Web MIDI output; the port has no MT-32 synth, ROMs or fallback).
- Input: keyboard and mouse. Joystick is reported absent.

## Working playable route (browser, verified by `npm run verify:browser`)

1. Original assets are loaded from `game/`, or from the user's folder in production.
2. Dynamix / Activision intro and credits.
3. Enter → sign-up page: type a name, click **GO FOR IT!**.
4. Copy-protection quiz (this build accepts any answer).
5. Car dealer (**TAKE THIS ONE**).
6. Hub (**FULL CIRCUIT RUN**).
7. Circuit (**GO RACIN'**).
8. Race in Seattle: accelerate with Up, steer with Left/Right, fire with Space.

Demo mode (`?args=demo`) autoplays the shop screens and a full race, then returns to the menus.

## Verification

| Command | What it checks | Level |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `npm run verify` | asset identity (92 hashes); 166 unit/module/scenario tests; closed-loop race replays (EGA and CGA) and segment comparisons | routine/segment + closed-loop |
| `npm run verify:browser` | real Chrome: boot → menus → race with real keyboard/mouse on EGA and on CGA (`?video=cga`); AdLib and MT-32 options (non-silent OPL output, MIDI bytes sent); fails on errors, diagnostics or missed milestones | browser acceptance |
| `node scripts/replay-race.mjs <dir> 0 399 --strict` | the replay alone, with per-range diffs | closed-loop |
| `node scripts/run-headless.mjs --args demo --seconds 120` | independent runtime scenario with the port's own environment providers, plus screenshots | independent scenario (no reference comparison) |

`npm run verify` needs the local game files, and the scenario test needs the local capture `.local/captures/demo-race-start` (recipe in `docs/scenarios/demo-race-start.json`). If either is missing, it fails with a setup error.

## Verified scenarios

- **demo-race-start**: 400 DOSBox checkpoints from race start.
  - The port runs the race loop closed-loop from checkpoint 0. **All 399 following checkpoints match exactly**: conventional memory except the documented ISR/sound/stack exclusions, and all four EGA planes.
  - Negative controls (one skipped RNG step, one altered byte) are detected.
  - Evidence is conditional on the injected start state; the race contained no interrupt-dependent stale read.

- **segment-race-setup**: `1000:32b8` (race setup: `.TRK`/`.MAP`/shape/bitmap loading and every DOS allocation) from a DOSBox entry checkpoint to its return. Memory and all four VRAM planes match exactly, including the MCB chain and its owner-name stamping rule, observed with `scripts/dosbox/trace-arena.mjs`. Segment-level evidence, conditional on the injected entry state.

- **sound-startup**: the MIDI bytes the MT-32 driver queues (first 692 equal DOSBox's 700 captured) and the AdLib register writes (299 of 299, plus the detection delay constants) from the program start. Times are not compared; audio is not compared.
- **cga-race-start**: 150 DOSBox checkpoints of a CGA demo race (`dtrack GC demo`). All 149 following frames match exactly: conventional memory, B800 RAM and the EGA planes. Same conditional-start caveat as demo-race-start.
- **cga-segments**: CGA driver init (`2fd2:0252`), hardware init (`2524:0260`, with five documented sound/joystick exclusions), ground fill (`2f73:035f`) and sky strip (`2f73:000f`) match DOSBox from injected entry states, memory and B800.

- **CGA display (one observation, not a committed test):** a paused DOSBox mode-6 screen (B800 RAM read through the API, frame from `/video/frame`) and `cgaFrame()` rendered from that RAM agree on all 128,000 pixels (9,013 lit). Mode 4 colours were not compared.

## Asset inspector

`viewer.html` now exposes the established resource formats: 179 image frames, 3 fonts, 3 EGA palettes, 10 skyline panoramas (60 strips), 10 road layouts/elevation profiles, 136 models (1,195 groups / 3,525 faces), 11 speaker effects, MIDI timelines, 88 title-script commands and 10 high-score records. Track object links open the referenced `shape.tbl` model. Effects reuse the translated `334e` interpreter and offer WAV export at each device's effect-tick rate.

`npm run audit:assets` validates these layouts against the local files, including all effect programs at three rates and track-to-model references. Inspector 3D rendering is orthographic/painter-order visualization, not the game renderer; MIDI audition remains simple synthesis. CGA palette data and save files retain raw inspection. Detailed coverage and limitations: [asset formats](asset-formats.md).

## Known limitations

- Speaker audio is approximate (inaudible rates above 15 kHz are silenced, one-pole low-pass).
- **Approximations** (all in `docs/re/environment.md`):
  - Timing model: race at 15 fps minimum, calibrated work costs.
  - `9542`'s interrupt-dependent stale stack word.
- Menu screens, shops, saves and results have **no reference comparison yet** (their RNG depends on timing). They are exercised by the demo and browser runs only.
- Tandy, Hercules/mode-4 and joystick paths are unsupported. Reaching one stops the game with a diagnostic (default strict mode) or is reported (`?mode=demo`).
- **CGA:** the title, menus and races are verified only as far as the captures above (race loop, sky, ground, driver init). The other driver slots (sprites, glyphs, lines, dissolve) are translated and checked against the original instructions by `tests/x86mini.mjs`, but not against DOSBox. Colour handling of mode 4 and the work-cost of B800 accesses (`work.vram` per byte) are APPROX; the menu timing on CGA is not calibrated.
- **Boot time:** with the MPU and OPL absent the port spends about 0.16 s of APPROX virtual time in the absent-device probes (docs/re/environment.md); the DOSBox references never ran that path.
- **AdLib:** synthesis is approximate (not bit-exact, no comparison with an OPL reference); the OPL port-access cost (2.4 µs) is fitted to one DOSBox count.
- **MT-32:** best with a connected MIDI output (real MT-32 or Munt) and Web MIDI permission. Without one (or with `?synth=builtin`) `src/web/midi-worklet.js` plays the same MIDI stream on a small built-in synth: APPROX, program numbers pick a rough instrument family, MT-32 SysEx timbres are ignored, so it does not sound like an MT-32. Byte times are not compared.
- No production deployment has been configured.

2. A capture with type-5 entities, to exercise the stale-slot input path.
